newsitem.title: INDIA: Former India minister faces arrest in graft case.
newsitem.headline: Former India minister faces arrest in graft case.

text.p: An Indian court on Monday issued an arrest warrant for an elusive former minister wanted in a corruption case after police last month discovered more than $1 million in cash and jewellery stashed in his homes.

Former communications minister Sukh Ram, who has been in London, is wanted for questioning by federal investigators and must appear before a local judge by October 1 under the terms of the warrant, officials said.
"It (the warrant) has to be executed. When and how is to be decided," S.M. Khan, spokesman for the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), told Reuters. "It may or may not be on (his) arrival."

Sukh Ram served in the cabinet of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, whose Congress party was beaten in general elections which ended in May. He spearheaded an ambitious drive to end the government's monopoly over telephone services.
Sukh Ram has repeatedly postponed his return to India since the surprise raids on his residences turned up the bundles of cash.
The CBI has accused him of pocketing kickbacks from a private firm which sold the government radio equipment, but the federal police agency has not filed any formal charges.
Sukh Ram has denied the accusations.
Khan said the CBI wanted to take Sukh Ram into custody for questioning.
After the warrant was issued, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported that the former minister had boarded an Air India flight to New Delhi on Monday and was expected to arrive overnight.
Newspapers have speculated that the government might cancel Sukh Ram's passport or seek his extradition if he failed to return soon to India.
Sukh Ram has denied accusations of corruption stemming from the discovery of some 36 million rupees ($1 million) in cash stuffed in suitcases and bags in two houses in New Delhi and nearby Ghaziabad.

"It was part of funds raised by the (Congress) party for electioneering," PTI quoted Sukh Ram on Monday as saying in London. "The money had been given to me by an important party functionary for party use in the election campaign to the Uttar Pradesh assembly."
Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state, holds assembly elections starting on September 30.
But the Congress party, which suspended Sukh Ram after the raids, has said the seized money did not belong to it.
The raids on Sukh Ram's homes marked the latest in a series of scandals that have hit the Congress party this year.
Authorities traced Sukh Ram to Britain a few days after the raids. But Sukh Ram, citing health problems, has put off his return to India.
